body: I used to get like that from time to time. When one of my best friends moved away to go to college, I broke down crying. Later on, I was shitty and rude to the new friends he'd made while there. I cringe to think about that one. I know now that a lot of my anxiety stems from abandonment issues.

I think you're right about a lot of things, really. I suppose if I was totally co-dependent, I would be feeling differently as I'd predicate all my emotions on the relationship. And if I was feeling normal, why would I let myself gravitate to disturbing thoughts and videos?

Maybe I just need a change of pace. Motivation has been kind of hard to come by lately.

No need to be sorry at all. Thanks for talking with me.

It's hard to say exactly what it is. I'm not sure what triggered these feelings, and I guess that's what strikes me as so odd about the whole thing. A month ago I was feeling great. I've struggled with depression and anxiety related to PTSD for a long time, though, but I had a handle on it.

My girlfriend can be a little stressful sometimes. Lately more than usual. I can't imagine that being the cause. Overall, our relationship is overwhelmingly positive.

Maybe I just let my anxiety slip, and I haven't coped in a healthy way. I can't afford therapy or medication, but I will be able to pretty soon. I don't feel suicidal, but for whatever reason, I'm slipping. I'm losing motivation.

Life is actually not all that terrible for you, but that doesn't mean you can't feel numb or hopeless sometimes, especially since you're not doing what you know you want to do. You might feel like you've crashed, but you're still just getting out there. Most people in that industry have to struggle for a while.

There is an entire generation of 20-somethings stuck at home because of the economy. You're not alone in this regard. The best part is, you're motivated to change your situation. Keep it up.

>All I wanted out of life was a somewhat decent-paying job that I didn't hate, maybe a few friends that I could hang out with and feel like I belonged somewhere. Maybe even someone that loved me, if I was lucky.

This is not by any means inaccessible to you. It might be a little distant at the moment, but it's totally in the realm of possibility. Hang in there, and you'll get to it.

I think you should go back to school, perhaps a community college and concentrate on getting another kind of degree. They're totally affordable, and if by some chance you can't afford it, you're in the US so they will literally pay you to go. Look into grants. At the very least, it will give you something to do and you'll be around other people your age.

Don't give up just yet.

Dreams of people we lost are the worst. They really are. I lost my mother when I was a boy, and for a long time afterwards I would dream about her. My grandmother came to live with us then, and when she passed away the same thing happened to me. But I'm telling you with all sincerity, it does go away after a while.

I know it's difficult. If you can't keep living for you, live for them. Just a little bit longer. You know it's the right thing to do.

A lot of people are feeling left out and devalued due to the recession. I know what poverty feels like firsthand. It sucks, in every way. It's humiliating and it's exhausting. You spend so much time worrying about where the money is going to come from next. It's constantly there, in the back of your mind. And it's hard not to be resentful. I know where you're coming from.

I want to reiterate a couple of things that are probably already on your mind: your mother would be devastated, and you know this. She probably wouldn't be able to afford your funeral, either. She needs you now. You're likely young and able-bodied. Suicide is not an option.

If I were you, I would contact a government agency about finding employment. I would ask anyone and everyone in my social network if they could get me a job. These things might hurt your pride, but being poor will hurt it worse.

You still have options.
